criteria.demonstration: The actual typed backing, allocator protocol, poison diagnostics and C object lifetime are separate. Requested-prefix observations use the baseline still-live arrays, not indeterminate pointers after deallocation. The wrapper tracks attempts, successful owners, upstream operations, logical live-cell peak and transient upstream overlap separately; counters saturate/refuse without obstructing cleanup. The actually inspected Rust GlobalAlloc passages bound the global-request optimization/reentry/resize comparison and are not relabeled ISO C rules.

criteria.demonstration: The V4Allocator declaration remains byte-identical to the actual containers.array producer. OaaAudit wraps that ABI with eight typed tracking slots, fail-at-N, requested-prefix poison and a separate upstream resize callback. Actual OwAllocator supplies copy-resize, and an original in-place provider changes the allocation assumption. Prefix preservation, newly initialized suffix, same-size attempted no-op, resize-failure owner/output preservation and accounting publication are explicit. Successful generic resize does not subsequently evaluate the old pointer.

criteria.criterion: Sweep every allocation failure point of frontier and COW workloads, fill all eight slots, test sizes0/16/17 and counter extrema, and verify requested-prefix poison plus release accounting. Compare the imported header byte for byte with the accepted ABI and reject the no-poison mutant. Integrate with the learner dynamic array and T65 error paths, measuring actual calls rather than inferring zero allocation from source spelling.

criteria.demonstration: Six C17 profiles execute seven anchors, six semantic compiled controls and seven compiling-stub rejections. The independent model checks19608two-owner histories with separate wrapper/upstream failure indices. Actual frontier and COW workloads sweep every backing acquisition; actual v4_reserve exercises retained state on failed growth. Tests cover eight-slot fullness, sizes0/16/17, counter extrema, cleanup after saturation, poison observed before upstream poison and full-upstream shrink refusal. Separate six-profile actual T65 Eop create/clone tests use zero-ID owning payloads, both allocation failure boundaries, independent backing and complete cleanup through the current counting allocator. Imports, stack/code sizes and seven cost samples retain exact source/toolchain identity.

criteria.demonstration: The delayed recursive allocation is implemented and measured. Actual T65 er_parse_pair makes zero allocator calls on the selected invalid input; the same error through a first-principles depth3 formatter makes three typed allocations, peaks at48live cells and cleans in reverse recursion order. Each formatting failure retains prior text. A reporter invoked after a consistent outer allocation failure can allocate independently through the same wrapper; nested attempts remain counted while nested failure reports are suppressed. The test distinguishes four attempts/one report from the two-attempt nested-upstream-failure case. Reporter contracts preserve the failed resize old owner and invoking borrows. Direct object import absence is explicitly insufficient for a whole-call-graph no-allocation claim. Independent delayed learner work remains unassessed.

limits: Externally serialized typed callbacks, not a global/concurrent allocator.
The two-owner oracle excludes recursive reporter and MAX-counter states; separate named tests cover those selected boundaries.
Reporter lifetime restrictions remain programmer obligations; raw C aliases are not revoked by poison.
Direct import audit does not prove no hidden callback allocation.
Published C17 inaccessible; no Rust compiler experiment or independent human/learner assessment.
